messages.author: 8d0a80872239233d
messages.subject: different detector devices
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently working with a dataset analysing rat density with three trapping sessions, each of them with three occasions, . Trapping devices were mostly Tomahawk traps, but in certain cases these were complemented with other devices (e.g.,  Sherman traps and handmade traps). The latter show much lower CPUE than Tomahawk traps (0.07 captures/trap-night and 0.01 captures/trap-night vs. 0.20 captures/trap-night ), yet some individuals were caught with them. Considering the huge difference in capture probability, I would like to know if there is a way to indicate to the model that different detecteros were used, so that it takes into account the different detection probability. Alternatively, what would happen if I include these detectors without considering capture probability differences? I guess the detection function should  be affected but I would appreciate any indication, particularly regarding the density output. Thank you in advance.

Best

Julien

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: different detector devices
parts: Simply define a detector-level covariate (presumably with 2 levels, Tomahawk and other) and use that in the model for g0 or lambda0.

Hi,

Here I am again. So I have been trying to specify time-varying detector covariates to SECR but I am stuck at "Error in value[[i]] : subscript out of bounds".

My dataset has 7 sessions (9 occasions each) and I specify the effort and the type of detector as a covariate (see attached files; separate files for each session and a single capthist file). SECR recognizes the existence of the covariates, whose name I can change with the argument "trapcovnames" from the following code (which BTW runs smoothly).

secr_data_dups<-read.capthist(captfile=paste0(folder_files,"/captfile_dups.txt"),trapfile=list.files(paste0(folder_files,"/trap_data_dups"),pattern=".txt",full.names = T),detector="single",fmt=c("trapID"),noncapt="NONE",noccasions = 9,verify=T,skip=1,binary.usage=F,trapcovnames = paste0("type",1:9)) # creating capthist data

Now, when I try to indicate those covariate columns are actually a single time varying covariate with the following code "timevaryingcov(covariates(traps(secr_data_dups)))<-list(type=1:9)", it returns the error I mentioned at the beginning of this message. Any suggestion on how to deal with this?

Thank you again,

Best

Hi again
I think you have tripped up over dealing with multiple sessions.
I haven't tried your particular example (didn't notice attachments at first), but it works with the ovenCH dataset below.
Murray

Something like this should work (given constant 9 occasions per session)
for (i in 1:7) timevaryingcov(covariates(traps(secr_data_dups[[i]]))) <- list(type = 1:9)

# test multi-session time-varying trap covariates
library(secr)

# generate some covariate data, assign separately for each session
# not needed in your case because covariate data are input from files
for (sess in 1:5) {
rand <- sample.int(2,44,replace = TRUE)  # nonsense values, 44 nets
covariates(traps(ovenCH[[sess]])) <- data.frame(matrix(rand, nrow = 44, ncol = ncol(ovenCH[[sess]])))
}

# again, assign separately for each session
for (sess in 1:5) {
timevaryingcov(traps(ovenCH[[sess]])) <- list(tvc = 1:ncol(ovenCH[[sess]]))
}

covariates(traps(ovenCH))
timevaryingcov(traps(ovenCH))

msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 25)
fit <- secr.fit(ovenCH, mask = msk, model = g0~tvc, trace = FALSE)

predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(tvc=c(1,2)))
$`tvc = 1` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.90997 0.125187 0.69578 1.19009 g0 logit 0.03113 0.004956 0.02276 0.04246 sigma log 78.45117 6.348505 66.96225 91.91129 $`tvc = 2` link estimate SE.estimate lcl ucl D log 0.90997 0.125187 0.6958 1.19009 g0 logit 0.02452 0.003991 0.0178 0.03368 sigma log 78.45117 6.348505 66.9622 91.91129

parts:
My reply contained an error, as can be seen from the actual example further down. It should have read -
for (i in 1:7) timevaryingcov(traps(secr_data_dups[[i]])) <- list(type = 1:9)

This allows 'type' to be used in model formulae (I checked). You will get into trouble using numeric codes for trap types (0,1,2,3 implies ascending numeric values). Character values will be treated automatically as factor levels, which is what you intend. (Incidentally, please format your code so it is readable; use spaces, indent, omit unnecessary arguments etc.).
